# Local flag prerequisites and environment overrides

2026-10-20. Implements the local prerequisite/environment portions of the original
UserFn specification's Flag model, SDK and Feature Flags sections. It extends
local bootstrap without claiming a configuration server, signed/ETag delivery,
background refresh or exposure transport.

## Configuration contract

TypeScript adds `FlagPrerequisite { key, expectedValue }`, optional
`FlagConfig.prerequisites`, `FlagEnvironmentOverride`, optional
`FlagConfig.environmentOverrides`, and `UserFnOptions.environment`. Python exposes
`FlagPrerequisite(key, expected_value)`, `FlagEnvironmentOverride`,
`FlagConfig.prerequisites`, `FlagConfig.environment_overrides`, and
`UserFnOptions.environment`. These are native SDK configuration types; this
checkpoint does not introduce a general camelCase/snake_case wire codec.

Every prerequisite must be available and its evaluated value must equal the
expected JSON value. Objects compare without key-order dependence; arrays remain
ordered; booleans, strings and numbers remain distinct. False, zero, empty strings,
arrays and objects are valid expected values. Python numeric comparison uses
finite float/IEEE-754 representation to match JavaScript JSON numbers, with
OverflowError/nonfinite rejection. Native Python arbitrary-precision integers
are outside shared exact numeric precision; encode exact large IDs as strings.
Tests distinguish the safe-integer boundary and confirm JavaScript rounding above
it. No string-to-number or boolean-to-number coercion is performed.

Missing, disabled, unmet and cyclic dependencies make the requested flag
unavailable: `getFlag/get_flag` returns that call's supplied fallback, not the
flag's configured default or a dependency's fabricated fallback. For example,
a missing dependency cannot satisfy `expectedValue: false`. This is not a forced
boolean false return: applications must choose an appropriate fallback for gated
features. Unrelated valid flags remain available. All prerequisites are ANDed.

Evaluation uses iterative DFS with per-call outcomes and cycle detection. It is
independent of definition insertion order and does not recurse through dependency
chains; 5,000-node chains are covered. Each dependency sees the same current user
and environment, and no outcome cache survives across users, identity resets,
configuration replacements or calls. Existing segments, inline constraints,
ordered rules, anonymous-user behavior and rollout percentage logic remain in
place. Environment is not added to the hash salt; a user's existing bucket stays
stable when an environment changes the percentage.

Environment names are exact, case-sensitive, nonempty strings. Missing/unknown
environments inherit the base flag. Only own TypeScript mapping entries are used,
including literal `__proto__` names; inherited `constructor`/`toString` entries
are never overrides. Overrides may replace `enabled`, `defaultValue`,
`defaultVariationId`, and the complete ordered rule array. Omitted fields inherit;
empty rule arrays explicitly replace base rules. Null/None for an override's
default variation explicitly clears it. Python uses an internal omission sentinel
to distinguish omitted default value/variation from explicit values; normal
construction does not require importing the sentinel. Base default variations
continue to take precedence unless replaced/cleared.

Base `enabled: false` remains a global kill switch: environment `enabled: true`
cannot resurrect it. An environment can additionally disable a globally enabled
flag. Variations and prerequisites are shared; overrides cannot remove dependency
gates or invent a second variation namespace.

## Validation and mutation boundaries

Definition replacement validates before modifying evaluator state. Invalid
replacements raise TypeError and preserve prior definitions. Duplicate/empty keys,
malformed prerequisite/override structures, unknown variation references,
out-of-range/nonfinite rollouts, unsupported constraint operators, cyclic JSON,
nonfinite values and unsupported value objects are rejected explicitly. Cycles or
missing nodes in the flag dependency graph are different: they are allowed to load
but resolve unavailable, supporting incomplete configurations without accidental
enablement. Known segment operators are preserved.

Loaded definitions are snapshotted. Modifying input objects after `setFlags` does
not change evaluation, and returned structured flag values are copied so they
cannot alter future prerequisite decisions. Caller-supplied fallback objects
retain their existing caller-owned behavior. Segments keep their existing
configuration contract; this change is not a general segment parity rewrite.

Operator save and enable-toggle paths use the same definition validator before
storage. The admin flag input/output schema now includes prerequisites,
environment overrides and the preexisting defaultVariationId field. Save, list
and global enable-toggle preserve them without dropping configuration. Tests use
the actual injected memory operator store and environment scope; this is not
proof of durable flag configuration storage. Shared dispatcher schemas are
validated explicitly; direct adapter invocation also reaches domain validation.

## Dependency and package closure

`@userfn/admin` now depends on the current shared `@superfunctions/admin` 0.1.5,
using local `@mcpfn/core` 0.0.6. A scoped npm workspace install and local builds
provided the actual dependencies. The root lock change is limited to the UserFn
admin dependency and removal of its obsolete nested admin/MCP/AJV graph; unrelated
npm optional/dev metadata churn was discarded. No shared source was changed.

A fresh installed CJS type consumer exposed the SDK's existing unconditional ESM
`types` export. Main and operator exports now select `.d.ts` for import and
`.d.cts` for require, matching the already generated runtime formats.

## Acceptance evidence

- TypeScript SDK source tests, production typecheck, CJS/ESM and declaration build.
- Python 3.9 source tests, plus a fresh built wheel installed in an isolated
  Python 3.12 environment; copied tests run against site-packages, without source
  pythonpath injection.
- Shared Unicode hash vectors and end-to-end environment-rollout prerequisites
  in both SDKs, including non-BMP and lone-surrogate IDs/keys. The separate
  [hash migration note](flag-hash-parity-readiness.md) documents changed Python
  non-BMP assignments; unchanged assignments are not claimed.
- Actual admin save/list/toggle and schema acceptance/rejection tests, typecheck
  and build with the local shared dependency closure.
- `typescript/scripts/verify-flag-context.mjs` packs SDK, UserFn admin, shared admin
  and MCP; installs all four tarballs in a fresh directory with normal dependency
  resolution; exercises ESM SDK/admin and CJS SDK runtime; then compiles installed
  `.mts` and `.cts` consumers under strict NodeNext without skipLibCheck or peer
  bypass. Temporary consumers are removed after the run.

Reproduce SDK/admin checks after building MCP/shared admin prerequisites:

```sh

npm test --prefix userfn/typescript
python3 -m pytest userfn/python/tests -q
npm run build --prefix userfn/typescript
npm test --prefix userfn/admin
npm run typecheck --prefix userfn/admin
npm run build --prefix userfn/admin
node userfn/typescript/scripts/verify-flag-context.mjs
```

## Remaining original requirements

Durable flag/config service storage, authenticated publish/fetch, signing and
ETag refresh, automatic refresh scheduling, exposure delivery, evaluation
telemetry, feature-flag UI/hooks, broader segment parity/operators, flag owner/tag
administration and deployed/browser/load acceptance remain open. Existing
messaging, surveys/forms, feedback source integrations, roadmap/changelog and
other original UserFn requirements are not completed by this local evaluator
checkpoint. Dependency gates are feature configuration, not an authorization
boundary replacing server-side access control.
EOF

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
```

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)

- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`

# Signed durable flag configuration service

2026-10-20. Implements the original specification's server storage and signed/
ETagged configuration publication boundary, reusing the shared HTTP/auth/database
abstractions. It does not complete the original flag SDK/analytics requirements.

## Behavior and storage

Optional host-provided Ed25519 private key and explicit key ID enable authenticated
`GET/PUT /config/:environment`. Readers and publishers require separate
`userfn:config:read/write` scopes. Trusted auth resolves tenant identity; payloads
cannot choose it. Permissions cover that tenant's environments. The function
wraps incoming adapters with its own schema, including the new
`userfn_flag_config` table. Hosts must migrate this table before enabling routes.
No adapterSchema escape hatch is required.

Complete flags/segments are runtime validated before storage, using the SDK flag
validator and existing supported segment constraints. JSON depth, canonical byte
size and item counts are bounded, in addition to the shared streamed request
limit. Malformed input cannot replace the current snapshot. Read and publish
operations authenticate before consuming the body.

Create requires If-None-Match:*; replacement requires the exact prior strong
If-Match value. Atomic database transactions and conditional update counts select
one winner. Missing conditions return428; stale/conflicting conditions return412.
Initial creation is protected by the table's unique identity. The current row
contains canonical wire bytes, ETag and signature; no private key is stored.
This is latest-version storage, not immutable revision-history storage.

Signatures cover exact UTF-8 response bytes, including fixed version/algorithm,
tenant, environment, UUID revision and signing-key identity. ETag hashes the same
bytes. A verifier must use an out-of-band trusted public-key map, reject unknown
key/algorithm/version, verify exact bytes and check expected tenant/environment.
Conditional304 responses reuse a previously verified snapshot; they do not
replace signature verification. Responses are private/revalidated and vary on
Authorization. Key rotation preserves old stored signatures until republishing.

## Evidence

- Six real local HTTP acceptance cases against actual file-backed SQLite through
  the shared Kysely adapter: signed byte/tamper verification, ETag/304, tenant and
  scope isolation, SQLite close/reopen, and competing writes through two separate
  SQLite connections (one200/one412; initial create one201/one412).
- Malformed JSON/config, missing/stale/invalid conditional headers and streamed
  oversized bodies reject without changing the accepted snapshot. Invalid signing
  configuration fails at construction. CORS exposes the conditional/signature
  headers only for configured origins.
- TS client evaluates the delivered flags/segments. Python performs real HTTP
  GET and evaluates prerequisite/environment values after explicit fixture mapping
  to native dataclasses. This fixture is not an SDK transport or verifier.
- Existing service10 tests and native feedback4 acceptance cases pass after the
  schema extension. Service typecheck/build pass; SDK build exposes the existing
  validator via its operator entry point. No shared source changes.

Reproduce after building the SDK and existing shared dependency closure:

```sh
npm run build --workspace userfn/typescript
npm run typecheck --workspace userfn/service
npm run build --workspace userfn/service
npm test --workspace userfn/service
npm run test:native --workspace userfn/service
```

## Original gates still open

Automatic SDK config fetch/signature verification, ETag-backed client cache and
refresh scheduling, refresh failure/rollback policy, signed-key distribution and
rotation administration, WatchFn exposures and evaluation telemetry, a durable
operator-store bridge/UI, owner/tag administration, broader segment parity and
operators, edge/CDN delivery and hosted/browser/load acceptance remain open.
Existing messaging, survey, feedback source, roadmap/changelog and all other
original requirements remain in scope. This checkpoint does not claim them ready.
EOF

public keys; the SDK environment is required and captured at construction. HTTPS
is mandatory unless the host explicitly enables local HTTP. Construction makes
no config request. TS uses WebCrypto; Python's `userfn[config]` optional extra

dependency-free.

verified snapshot, false for 304 reuse. Concurrent calls coalesce. Responses are
bounded by 264KiB, 4096 read chunks, 20 JSON levels and an overall request deadline

compressed responses reject before body consumption. Redirects and ambient
cookies are disabled; Python also disables environment proxy settings.

expected tenant/environment, known pinned key ID and SHA-256 ETag. Only then are
all flag/segment definitions validated and staged. Both are applied without an
await between them. Python maps the actual service wire representation into
native dataclasses, preserving rules/prerequisites/environment overrides. Loaded
key mappings are copied; response-provided keys are never trusted.

configuration. 304 cannot establish a cache: it requires the existing verified
ETag and unchanged local definitions. Successful manual configuration setters
invalidate ETag reuse and prevent an older in-flight request overwriting the

  against the installed service, with no source aliases. Strict installed service
  declarations remain checked without skipLibCheck/peer bypass.

refresh lifecycle/backoff, persistent client caching, monotonic replay/rollback
and freshness policy, key distribution/revocation administration, browser-native
acceptance, WatchFn flag exposures/evaluation telemetry, UI/hooks and broader
segment/operator parity remain open. A valid signature proves authenticity, not
that a server returned its newest revision; revision UUIDs are not monotonic.
Messaging, surveys, feedback integrations, roadmap/changelog and all other
original requirements are unaffected and remain in scope.

addition to preventing late application.

userfn/service/README.md:3:`@userfn/service` provides the dedicated feedback persistence path through shared HTTP, auth and database abstractions. It is a Node ESM package. Consumers provide the HTTP framework adapter and database connection; this package does not re-export or duplicate them.
userfn/service/README.md:33:The service wraps the incoming shared adapter with its own schema. Create the actual `userfn_feedback` table before serving traffic; `id` must have a primary-key/unique constraint for race-safe idempotency. `getUserFnSchema()` exposes fields and indexes. This package does not create tables, close caller-owned adapters or claim that a memory adapter is durable. Idempotency lasts while its row is retained; no TTL/retention worker is implemented.
userfn/service/README.md:37:Run `npm test --workspace=@userfn/service` for service contract tests, `npm run test:native --workspace=@userfn/service` for file-backed SQLite, actual loopback HTTP, and both SDKs, and `npm run test:authfn --workspace=@userfn/service` for real AuthFn issuance/revocation through its provider. The latter uses AuthFn memory storage and UserFn file-backed SQLite; it does not prove durable AuthFn credentials. userfn/service/README.md:45:`POST /feedback/:id/vote` takes `{direction: -1 | 0 | 1}` and requires `userfn:feedback:vote`. Anonymous voting is not enabled, and merely sharing a tenant credential does not establish individual users.
userfn/service/README.md:73:Each bounded batch (1–500 rows) commits normalized data and a persisted cursor together. Failed batches roll back; rerunning resumes from the last committed cursor. New submissions atomically write feedback and normalized rows through shared DB transactions; adapters without transaction support fail closed. An empty installation still needs the migration call to mark filters ready. Restoring/importing legacy rows after completion or running multiple migration workers is outside this migration contract.
userfn/service/README.md:77:When the requested page fills within a chunk, `nextCursor` is the last returned match, preserving all unreturned matches. When the scan budget ends first, `nextCursor` advances past the consumed candidates and the page may be partial or empty. Continue until `nextCursor === null`; never stop merely because an item list is empty or shorter than `limit`. A full final page may be followed by one empty terminal page. Keep filters unchanged during traversal. More than500 matching rows are traversable across requests without truncation or a candidate-overflow503. cat > userfn/.conduct/flag-config-scheduling-readiness.md <<'EOF'
# Explicit background configuration refresh lifecycle

2026-10-20. Adds the original background-refresh requirement on top of the verified
service/SDK contract, with explicit lifecycle ownership in both languages.

## Behavior

`startConfigRefresh/start_config_refresh` starts one immediate refresh and is
idempotent while running. `refreshInterval/refresh_interval` is milliseconds,
default30000, valid100–86400000. Python requires a running asyncio loop and rejects
without leaking a coroutine or marking itself running when none exists.
Constructors remain network-free. Subsequent requests begin only after settlement
plus delay; explicit refresh calls coalesce with the active request.

Failures preserve last-good values and are observable in a copied status record:
running state, consecutive failures, last error, last-success epoch milliseconds
and next scheduled epoch milliseconds. Backoff doubles per failure and caps at
five minutes or the configured interval when longer. Verified success/304 resets
the delay. Status contains fixed transport errors, not response bodies or keys.

Awaitable stop disables scheduling, synchronously fences active work before
yielding, cancels it and awaits settlement. Verified ETag state survives restart;
manual setters still invalidate it. Await stop before start to prevent overlapping
lifecycle transitions. Stop also cancels explicit callers sharing active transport
work. Permanent close prevents restart. TS close is awaitable; Python preserves
its synchronous close fence, with awaitable stop for settlement. Node timers are
unref'ed so this optional loop alone does not keep the process alive.

## Acceptance

- Four deterministic TS scheduler tests cover idempotent start, interval, capped
  backoff/reset, no overlap, cancellation settlement and timer cleanup.
- Actual service HTTP tests cover repeated conditional refresh, stop/restart,
  retained ETag, active-request stop and no late application. Python real HTTP
  tests cover the same lifecycle, observable failure and invalid/synchronous start.
- Updated actual Chrome and installed-package checks exercise start/stop as well
  as verified refresh. Final counts/results are recorded after final validation.

## Remaining original requirements

Durable client caches, monotonic signed revision/freshness/rollback policy, key
rotation/revocation administration, jitter/fleet/load acceptance, cross-browser
and hosted HTTPS acceptance, WatchFn exposure delivery, flag UI/hooks, owner/tag
administration, broader segment/operator parity and all other original UserFn
requirements remain open. Background scheduling is not exposure delivery or a
claim of complete platform readiness.
EOF

key administration and exposure requirements remain open.
EOF","workdir":"/Volumes/Dev/n/worktrees/superfunctions/userfn-sf-next-readiness","max_output_tokens":500}

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

# Clear cache
turbo run clean
```

## 📚 Important Files

### Root Configuration

- `package.json` - Workspace and script definitions
- `turbo.json` - Turbo build configuration
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript base config (if exists)

### Package Configuration

- `package.json` - Package metadata, dependencies, scripts
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `vitest.config.ts` - Test configuration
- `pyproject.toml` - Python package configuration

### Documentation

- `README.md` - Package overview and usage
- `SPEC.md` - Technical specification (common in larger functions)
- `.conduct/*.md` - Implementation plans, audits, tasks

## 🔍 Finding Code

### Search Patterns

- **Function implementations**: `{function}/typescript/src/` or `{function}/python/{function}/`
- **Tests**: `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`
- **Types**: `types.ts`, `models.py`, `src/types/`
- **Adapters**: `packages/http-*/`, `packages/python-*/`, `adapters/`
- **Examples**: `examples/`, `{function}/examples/`

### Key Directories

```
superfunctions/
├── {function}/              # Core function packages
│   ├── typescript/          # TS implementation
│   ├── python/              # Python implementation
│   ├── .conduct/            # Artifacts
│   ├── README.md            # Documentation
│   └── SPEC.md              # Specification (if exists)
├── packages/                # Shared packages
│   ├── {name}/              # @superfunctions/{name}
│   └── python-{name}/       # Python shared packages
└── _conduct/                # Root artifacts
```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

## 🔗 Related Resources

- **Repository**: https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions
- **License**: MIT (most packages) / Apache-2.0 (some packages)
- **Organization**: 21n
- **Contact**: hello@21n.org

## 📝 Notes for AI Agents

1. **Always check both TypeScript and Python** implementations when working on core functions
2. **Respect the naming conventions** - shared packages use `@superfunctions/`, functions use simple names
3. **Create artifacts in `.conduct/` folders**, not in root or arbitrary locations
4. **Avoid nested monorepos** - use subfolders within the main Turbo monorepo
5. **Use Turbo commands** for cross-package operations
6. **Check existing patterns** in similar functions before implementing new features
7. **Maintain consistency** across TypeScript and Python SDKs
8. **Update workspaces** in root `package.json` when adding new packages
9. **Follow existing test patterns** (Vitest for TS, pytest for Python)
10. **Document thoroughly** - this is a developer-focused ecosystem

# AGENTS.md - AI Agent Development Guide for Superfunctions

> **Purpose**: This document provides AI agents with essential information for working effectively on the Superfunctions monorepo.

## 🏗️ Repository Structure

Superfunctions is a **Turbo monorepo** containing self-hosted developer tools and libraries. The repository is organized into:

### Core Functions (Top-Level Directories)

Individual superfunction packages, each providing specific developer capabilities:

- **`authfn/`** - Authentication & API key management
- **`cachefn/`** - Multi-tier caching with function memoization
- **`drawfn/`** - Cross-framework drawing canvas for brainstorming
- **`plugfn/`** - Integration platform (OAuth, webhooks, 75+ providers)
- **`searchfn/`** - Browser-first full-text search with IndexedDB
- **`secfn/`** - Security functions (secrets vault, rate limiting, monitoring)
- **`testfn/`** - Testing utilities and frameworks
- **`botfn/`** - Bot framework (Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations)
- **`hostfn/`** - Hosting and deployment utilities
- **`uifn/`** - UI components and utilities
- **`watchfn/`** - File watching and monitoring
- **`billfn/`** - Billing and payment processing
- **`browsefn/`** - Browser automation utilities
- **`chartfn/`** - Charting and visualization
- **`datafn/`** - Data processing utilities
- **`docsfn/`** - Documentation generation
- **`filefn/`** - File operations and management
- **`flowfn/`** - Flow control (queues, streams, workflows)
- **`iconfn/`** - Icon utilities
- **`logfn/`** - Logging utilities
- **`mailfn/`** - Programmable real inboxes for products, agents, and tests
- **`sendfn/`** - Email/messaging utilities

### Shared Packages (`packages/`)

Framework-agnostic core libraries used across superfunctions:

**TypeScript Packages:**

- `@superfunctions/http` - HTTP abstractions
- `@superfunctions/http-express` - Express.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-fastify` - Fastify adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-hono` - Hono adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-next` - Next.js adapter
- `@superfunctions/http-sveltekit` - SvelteKit adapter
- `@superfunctions/db` - Database adapter system (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- `@superfunctions/auth` - Authentication abstraction layer
- `@superfunctions/cli` - CLI tool for schema management

**Python Packages:**

- `superfunctions` (from `python-core/`) - Core namespace package
- `superfunctions-sqlalchemy` (from `python-sqlalchemy/`)
- `superfunctions-fastapi` (from `python-fastapi/`)
- `superfunctions-flask` (from `python-flask/`)

### Other Directories

- **`_conduct/`** - Root-level artifacts for shared code (implementation plans, specs, audits)
- **`21n/`** - Organization-specific packages
- **`.agent/`** - Agent workflows and automation
- **`.github/`** - GitHub Actions and CI/CD

## 📦 Package Naming Conventions

### Rule A: Shared Packages Format

**Any package shared across superfunctions uses `@superfunctions/{name}` format**

Examples:

```
packages/db/          → @superfunctions/db
packages/http/        → @superfunctions/http
packages/auth/        → @superfunctions/auth
packages/cli/         → @superfunctions/cli
```

### Rule B: Core Function Packages Format

**Single-package functions**: Use simple name without scope

```
authfn/ts-sdk/        → authfn
drawfn/core/          → drawfn
cachefn/typescript/   → cachefn
plugfn/core/         → plugfn
searchfn/             → searchfn
```

**Multi-package functions**: Use `@{functionname}/{sub-package}` format (if needed in future)

```
@authfn/core          (example for future multi-package structure)
@authfn/providers     (example for future multi-package structure)
```

**Current Status**: All core functions currently use single-package structure. The scoped format is reserved for future expansion if a function needs multiple published packages.

### Rule C: Monorepo Structure

**The root `superfunctions` is a Turbo monorepo. Avoid nested monorepos.**

- ✅ Use subfolders to organize functions (e.g., `authfn/python/`, `authfn/ts-sdk/`)
- ❌ Do NOT create nested monorepos (e.g., `authfn/` should NOT be another monorepo)
- ✅ Use Turbo workspaces defined in root `package.json`

Current workspaces:

```json
{
  "workspaces": [
    "searchfn",
    "botfn/*",
    "hostfn/*",
    "authfn/*",
    "packages/*",
    "21n/*"
  ]
}
```

### Rule D: Artifact Location

**Create artifacts (`.md` files) in `.conduct` folders**

- **Function-specific artifacts**: `{function}/.conduct/`
  - Examples: `authfn/.conduct/implementation.md`, `drawfn/.conduct/audit_report.md`
- **Shared/root artifacts**: `_conduct/`
  - Examples: `_conduct/implementation.md`, `_conduct/spec.md`

Artifact types:

- `implementation.md` - Implementation plans
- `spec.md` - Technical specifications
- `audit_report.md` - Code audits and reviews
- `task.md` - Task tracking
- `walkthrough.md` - Feature walkthroughs

## 🗂️ Language Support

Most core functions support **both TypeScript and Python**:

### TypeScript Structure

```
{function}/
├── typescript/       or  core/
│   ├── src/
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── tsconfig.json
│   └── vitest.config.ts
```

### Python Structure

```
{function}/
├── python/
│   ├── {function}/        # Python package directory
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── tests/
│   ├── pyproject.toml
│   └── README.md
```

### Examples

- `authfn/typescript/` + `authfn/python/`
- `cachefn/typescript/` + `cachefn/python/`
- `secfn/typescript/` + `secfn/python/`
- `plugfn/core/` + `plugfn/python/`
- `drawfn/core/` (TypeScript only, with React/Svelte adapters)
- `searchfn/` (TypeScript only, browser-focused)

## 🔧 Development Workflow

### Building

```bash
# Build all packages
npm run build

# Build specific package (from root)
turbo run build --filter=authfn
turbo run build --filter=@superfunctions/db

# Build from package directory
cd authfn/ts-sdk && npm run build
```

### Testing

```bash
# Test all packages
npm test

# Test specific package
turbo run test --filter=drawfn

# Watch mode
npm run test:watch
```

### Linting

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Package Manager

- **npm** (v10.2.0+) - Specified in `packageManager` field
- Uses npm workspaces for monorepo management
- Turbo for build orchestration

## 🎯 Key Superfunctions Features

### AuthFn

- Multi-provider authentication (OAuth, API keys, JWT)
- Framework-agnostic with adapters for Express, Fastify, Hono, Next.js, SvelteKit
- Database-agnostic (Drizzle, Prisma, Kysely)
- TypeScript + Python SDKs

### DrawFn

- Cross-framework drawing canvas
- React and Svelte adapters
- Scene management, export capabilities
- Tolerant parsing with version validation

### PlugFn

- Self-hosted integration platform
- 75+ provider integrations (GitHub, Slack, Discord, Linear, Stripe)
- OAuth 2.0 flow handling
- Webhook support
- Multi-tenant with secure token storage

### SearchFn

- Browser-first full-text search
- IndexedDB persistence with in-memory LRU cache
- BM25 scoring
- FlexSearch-compatible API
- Worker-ready with snapshot export/import

### MailFn

- Stable and expiring programmable inboxes
- Cloudflare Email Workers, D1, R2, and Queues deployment adapter
- Raw MIME and attachment evidence, waits, OTP/link extraction, threads, labels, and search
- Typed client, test helpers, CLI, MCP server, custom domains, webhooks, and SendFn composition
- Scoped credentials, retention, audit, quotas, and explicitly gated public-platform controls

### CacheFn

- Multi-tier caching (memory, IndexedDB, external)
- Function memoization
- TTL and invalidation strategies
- Browser and server support

### SecFn

- Secrets vault management
- Access control and permissions
- Rate limiting
- Security monitoring
- Secret scanning

### BotFn

- Multi-platform bot framework
- Discord, GitHub, Linear integrations
- Shared types and persistence layer
- Event-driven architecture

## 🛠️ Common Tasks

### Adding a New Function

1. Create top-level directory: `{functionname}/`
2. Add TypeScript SDK: `{functionname}/typescript/` or `{functionname}/ts-sdk/`
3. (Optional) Add Python SDK: `{functionname}/python/`
4. Create `.conduct/` for artifacts
5. Add to workspace in root `package.json`
6. Package name: `{functionname}` (not scoped unless multi-package)

### Adding a Shared Package

1. Create in `packages/{name}/`
2. Package name: `@superfunctions/{name}`
3. Add to workspace (already covered by `packages/*`)
4. Update dependent packages

### Creating Artifacts

1. Function-specific: `{function}/.conduct/{artifact}.md`
2. Shared/root: `_conduct/{artifact}.md`
3. Use consistent naming: `implementation.md`, `spec.md`, `audit_report.md`, etc.

### Working with Turbo

```bash
# Run task across all packages
turbo run build
turbo run test

# Run for specific package
turbo run build --filter=authfn

# Run with dependencies
turbo run build --filter=authfn...

# Clear cache
turbo run clean
```

## 📚 Important Files

### Root Configuration

- `package.json` - Workspace and script definitions
- `turbo.json` - Turbo build configuration
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript base config (if exists)

### Package Configuration

- `package.json` - Package metadata, dependencies, scripts
- `tsconfig.json` - TypeScript configuration
- `vitest.config.ts` - Test configuration
- `pyproject.toml` - Python package configuration

### Documentation

- `README.md` - Package overview and usage
- `SPEC.md` - Technical specification (common in larger functions)
- `.conduct/*.md` - Implementation plans, audits, tasks

## 🔍 Finding Code

### Search Patterns

- **Function implementations**: `{function}/typescript/src/` or `{function}/python/{function}/`
- **Tests**: `__tests__/`, `tests/`, `*.test.ts`, `test_*.py`
- **Types**: `types.ts`, `models.py`, `src/types/`
- **Adapters**: `packages/http-*/`, `packages/python-*/`, `adapters/`
- **Examples**: `examples/`, `{function}/examples/`

### Key Directories

```
superfunctions/
├── {function}/              # Core function packages
│   ├── typescript/          # TS implementation
│   ├── python/              # Python implementation
│   ├── .conduct/            # Artifacts
│   ├── README.md            # Documentation
│   └── SPEC.md              # Specification (if exists)
├── packages/                # Shared packages
│   ├── {name}/              # @superfunctions/{name}
│   └── python-{name}/       # Python shared packages
└── _conduct/                # Root artifacts
```

## 🚀 Best Practices

### Super functions ecosystem (Very important)

- Reuse shared packages from `packages/` folder like http abstraction, db abstraction, etc.
- Never duplicate shared code like http adapters, db abstractions, etc.
- Don't reexport http-adapters etc - end consumers of the core function package will use the adapters directly. Refer `authfn` implementation for usage of core http router, core db, http adapters and db interface usage.
- Function packages that accept a `@superfunctions/db` `Adapter` must wrap the incoming adapter internally with their own schema, for example `wrapWithSchema(config.database, getSchema(...))`, before passing it to services/storage. Do not require app consumers to pass `adapterSchema` to `drizzleAdapter`, `kyselyAdapter`, `prismaAdapter`, or `memoryAdapter`; `adapterSchema` is a deprecated compatibility escape hatch for direct app-level adapter use.

### Code Organization

- Keep shared code in `packages/`
- Keep function-specific code in `{function}/`
- Use TypeScript for type safety
- Provide Python SDKs for backend-focused functions
- Write comprehensive tests

### Documentation

- Update README.md with usage examples
- Create SPEC.md for complex functions
- Document breaking changes
- Keep artifacts in `.conduct/` folders

### Testing

- Use Vitest for TypeScript
- Use pytest for Python
- Maintain high test coverage
- Test adapters separately

### Versioning

- Follow semantic versioning
- Coordinate versions across language SDKs
- Document migration guides for breaking changes

## 🔗 Related Resources

- **Repository**: https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions
- **License**: MIT (most packages) / Apache-2.0 (some packages)
- **Organization**: 21n
- **Contact**: hello@21n.org

## 📝 Notes for AI Agents

1. **Always check both TypeScript and Python** implementations when working on core functions
2. **Respect the naming conventions** - shared packages use `@superfunctions/`, functions use simple names
3. **Create artifacts in `.conduct/` folders**, not in root or arbitrary locations
4. **Avoid nested monorepos** - use subfolders within the main Turbo monorepo
5. **Use Turbo commands** for cross-package operations
6. **Check existing patterns** in similar functions before implementing new features
7. **Maintain consistency** across TypeScript and Python SDKs
8. **Update workspaces** in root `package.json` when adding new packages
9. **Follow existing test patterns** (Vitest for TS, pytest for Python)
10. **Document thoroughly** - this is a developer-focused ecosystem

# Explicit background configuration refresh lifecycle

2026-10-20. Adds the original background-refresh requirement on top of the verified
service/SDK contract, with explicit lifecycle ownership in both languages.

## Behavior

`startConfigRefresh/start_config_refresh` starts one immediate refresh and is
idempotent while running. `refreshInterval/refresh_interval` is milliseconds,
default30000, valid100–86400000. Python requires a running asyncio loop and rejects
without leaking a coroutine or marking itself running when none exists.
Constructors remain network-free. Subsequent requests begin only after settlement
plus delay; explicit refresh calls coalesce with the active request.

Failures preserve last-good values and are observable in a copied status record:
running state, consecutive failures, last error, last-success epoch milliseconds
and next scheduled epoch milliseconds. Backoff doubles per failure and caps at
five minutes or the configured interval when longer. Verified success/304 resets
the delay. Status contains fixed transport errors, not response bodies or keys.

Awaitable stop disables scheduling, synchronously fences active work before
yielding, cancels it and awaits settlement. Verified ETag state survives restart;
manual setters still invalidate it. Await stop before start to prevent overlapping
lifecycle transitions. Stop also cancels explicit callers sharing active transport
work. Permanent close prevents restart. TS close is awaitable; Python preserves
its synchronous close fence, with awaitable stop for settlement. Node timers are
unref'ed so this optional loop alone does not keep the process alive.

## Acceptance

- Four deterministic TS scheduler tests cover idempotent start, interval, capped
  backoff/reset, no overlap, cancellation settlement and timer cleanup.
- Actual service HTTP tests cover repeated conditional refresh, stop/restart,
  retained ETag, active-request stop and no late application. Python real HTTP
  tests cover the same lifecycle, observable failure and invalid/synchronous start.
- Updated actual Chrome and installed-package checks exercise start/stop as well
  as verified refresh. Final counts/results are recorded after final validation.

## Remaining original requirements

Durable client caches, monotonic signed revision/freshness/rollback policy, key
rotation/revocation administration, jitter/fleet/load acceptance, cross-browser
and hosted HTTPS acceptance, WatchFn exposure delivery, flag UI/hooks, owner/tag
administration, broader segment/operator parity and all other original UserFn
requirements remain open. Background scheduling is not exposure delivery or a
claim of complete platform readiness.

from .core.config_refresh import ConfigRefreshLoop
from .core.config_http import HttpConfigService, ConfigRefreshError
from typing import Optional, List, Any
from .types import UserFnOptions, FlagValue, FlagConfig, UserTraits, Campaign, Survey, FeedbackSubmission
from .core.identity import IdentityManager
from .core.feedback import FeedbackEngine
from .core.feedback_http import HttpFeedbackService
from .core.flags import FlagEvaluator
from .core.segments import SegmentEvaluator
from .core.messaging import MessagingEngine

class UserFnClient:
    def __init__(self, options: UserFnOptions):
        self.options = options
        self._config_environment = options.environment
        self._config_refresh_loop = None
        self.config_service = HttpConfigService(options) if options.config else None
        self.identity = IdentityManager()
        self.feedback = FeedbackEngine(options.feedback_service if options.feedback_service is not None else (HttpFeedbackService(options) if options.endpoint else None), self.identity.get_user)
        self.segments = SegmentEvaluator()
        self.flags = FlagEvaluator([], self.segments, options.environment)
        self.messaging = MessagingEngine(self.segments)
        # self.surveys = SurveyEngine(self.segments) # TODO: Implement SurveyEngine

        self.flags.set_flags([
            FlagConfig(key=key, default_value=value, variations=[], rules=[], enabled=True)
            for key, value in (options.bootstrap_flags or {}).items()
        ])

    def identify(self, id: str, traits: Optional[UserTraits] = None):
        self.identity.identify(id, traits)

    def reset(self):
        self.identity.reset()

    def get_flag(self, key: str, default_value: FlagValue = False) -> FlagValue:
        user = self.identity.get_user()
        return self.flags.get_flag(key, default_value, user)

    # Messaging
    def trigger(self, trigger_type: str, context: str) -> List[Campaign]:
        """
        Check for eligible campaigns. 
        Returns list of eligible campaigns (unlike TS which usually renders them).
        """
        user = self.identity.get_user()
        return self.messaging.get_eligible_messages(trigger_type, context, user)

    # Configuration setters (normally loaded from server)
    async def refresh_config(self) -> bool:
        if not self.config_service:
            raise ConfigRefreshError('Signed configuration is not configured')
        def apply(flags, segments):
            evaluator = FlagEvaluator(flags, self.segments, self._config_environment)
            self.segments.set_segments(segments)
            self.flags = evaluator
        return await self.config_service.refresh(apply)

    def close_config(self):
        """Permanently close config transport; in-flight work cannot apply later."""

# Flag exposure delivery

2026-10-20. Implements the original flag exposure requirement using selected
branch provenance and actual Watch ingestion. Both SDKs preserve their synchronous
flag-value API. Configuration is opt-in and separate from the UserFn service key.

The evaluator carries value, variation ID, rule ID and reason from the selected
branch through prerequisite resolution; it never infers IDs by comparing values.
Only the requested public flag emits. Constructor bootstrap values have a distinct
reason until a successful definition replacement. Unavailable flags use the caller
fallback with null IDs. Returned configured JSON values remain isolated copies.

TypeScript uses the current `@watchfn/browser` capture/flush implementation with
`autoTrack:false`, no sampling and no automatic retry loop. Python supplies a
bounded direct HTTP transport via optional `httpx`; synchronous evaluation only
enqueues and explicit async flush performs delivery. Both use canonical Watch
track envelopes, stable UUID event identities, fixed error messages, bounded
queue/event/batch size and request deadlines. No flag values, traits or credentials
are included in event properties. HTTPS is default; local HTTP requires opt-in.

Delivery failures retain queued events. Overflow and oversized captures count as
dropped without changing the flag result, and the next explicit flush reports
rejected captures once. Close fences capture immediately while draining; failed
close/flush can be retried. Neither queue is durable. Ordinary Watch event ingestion
is at least once; ambiguous response loss can cause duplicate stored rows even
though retry preserves the event ID.

## Validation

Focused provenance and transport tests cover equal-valued variations, prerequisite
root-only events, environment/default/bootstrap/unavailable branches, full queues,
oversized metadata, failure retention, stable identity, close and coalesced flush.
Actual built Watch HTTP/SQLite/browser acceptance is recorded separately in
`exposure-acceptance-readiness.md`. The full TS SDK suite passes 77 tests; Python 3.9 source and fresh installed
Python 3.12.12 wheel with config/exposures extras each pass 79 tests. A core-only
fresh wheel imports and evaluates without optional HTTP/crypto dependencies.
SDK typecheck/build pass; service native HTTP/SQLite suite passes 16 tests after
the Watch merge. Fresh npm tarballs include the actual Watch browser package;
installed HTTP exposure/config/scheduler runtime and strict declarations pass
without peer bypass or skipLibCheck.

## Remaining original requirements

Watch credentials are not tenant-scoped or ingestion-only; deployment needs a
trusted proxy or appropriate isolation. Durable offline exposure storage,
exactly-once ingestion, consent/privacy administration and fleet/load evidence
remain open. Exposure delivery does not implement messaging/survey delivery,
UI/hooks, owner/tag administration, durable config caches, key revocation,
monotonic config rollback policy or all original UserFn requirements.

# UserFn Specification (Draft)

Last updated: 2026-01-14  
Status: Draft (implementation not started)  
Owner: Platform (Superfunctions)

## Goal
Build `userfn`, a self-hosted user engagement platform covering in-app messaging (Intercom-style), surveys/forms, feature flags, feedback boards (Canny-style with unified sources), roadmap, and changelog—leveraging existing Superfunctions primitives (`watchfn`, `botfn`, `plugfn`, `authfn`, `drawfn`, shared packages).

## Scope (v1)
- Identity & traits with segmentation.
- Feature flags: deterministic eval, rollouts, prerequisites, kill switches, typed SDKs.
- In-app messaging: campaigns, banners/modals/tooltips/inbox, targeting, throttling, impressions/clicks tracking.
- Surveys/forms: NPS/CSAT/CES/custom; branching; throttling; submissions stored as structured events.
- Feedback board: voting, statuses, tags; unified ingestion from in-app + Discord + GitHub Discussions + Discourse + email/web form.
- Roadmap: public view backed by feedback links.
- Changelog: in-app “What’s new”, RSS/webhook.
- Analytics: reuse `watchfn` for events (impressions, clicks, exposures, survey responses).

## Non-Goals (v1)
- Native mobile SDKs (web first; RN later).
- Full-blown CRM; focus on product-facing engagement.
- Billing/entitlements (reuse existing infra later).

## Architecture
- Client SDK (`userfn/typescript`): identity, flags, messaging renderer, surveys, feedback submission; React/Svelte helpers.
- Server service (`userfn/service`): REST/tRPC (uses `@superfunctions/http`, `@superfunctions/db`); stores config (flags, campaigns, surveys, feedback board, roadmap, changelog).
- Transport/analytics: reuse `watchfn` ingestion for runtime events; dedicated service endpoints for config CRUD and feedback/roadmap data.
- Integrations: `botfn` for Discord + issue trackers; `plugfn`/webhooks for GitHub Discussions, Discourse.
- UI: lightweight embeddable components; themeable; accessible.

## Data Model (high level)
- User: `id`, `traits` (plan, role, region, locale), `createdAt`, `lastSeenAt`.
- Segment: rules over traits/events (operators: equals/contains/in/regex/range/time/geo).
- Flag: `key`, `variations`, `default`, `rules` (segments, % rollout, prerequisites, env overrides, kill switch), `tags`, `owner`.
- Campaign: `id`, `kind` (banner/modal/tooltip/inbox), `content`, `audience` (segments), `triggers` (url match, event, flag), `schedule`, `priority`, `caps` (per-user, global), `dismissible`.
- Delivery state: per-user per-campaign `status` (eligible/shown/clicked/dismissed), `timestamps`.
- Survey: `id`, `type` (NPS/CSAT/CES/custom), `questions` (branching optional), `audience`, `frequency cap`, `start/end`, `cta`.
- SurveyResponse: `user`, `answers`, `score`, `submittedAt`.
- Feedback: `id`, `title`, `body`, `source` (in_app/discord/github_discussion/discourse/email/form), `status` (open/planned/in_progress/done/closed), `tags`, `productArea`, `votes`, `linkedIssues` (GitHub/Linear), `linkedRoadmapItems`, `createdBy`, `attachments?`, `duplicates?`.
- RoadmapItem: `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, `owner`, `ETA?`, `linkedFeedback[]`, `linkedFlags[]`.
- ChangelogEntry: `id`, `title`, `body`, `tags`, `publishedAt`, `relatedFlags`, `relatedRoadmapItems`.

## SDKs (TS browser, Node; Python later)
- Identity: `userfn.identify({ id, traits })`, `reset()`.
- Flags:
  - `getFlag(key, default)`, `useFlag` hook; typed variations.
  - Bootstrap payload + local cache; background refresh with ETag.
  - Emit exposure events to `watchfn`.
  - Deterministic bucketing (userId/sessionId hash), prerequisites, env overrides.
- Messaging:
  - `userfn.render(slotId)` to hydrate widgets; components for banner/modal/tooltip/inbox.
  - Triggering from campaigns; dedupe, caps, priority.
  - Track impressions, clicks, dismissals via `watchfn`.
- Surveys:
  - `openSurvey(id)` / inline render; validators; submission with throttling; responses sent as structured events and stored in service.
- Feedback:
  - `submitFeedback({ title, body, tags, attachments? })`; optional screenshot+annotation via `drawfn`; source = `in_app`.
  - Votes: `voteFeedback(id, dir)`.
- Server/Edge (Node):
  - Flag evaluation (for SSR/edge) using same rules engine; bootstrap API client.
  - Webhooks client for ingesting external feedback events (Discord, GitHub, Discourse).

## In-App Messaging
- Campaign definition: audience (segments), triggers (URL glob/regex, event name, flag on/off), schedule (start/end), priority, frequency caps (per-user, per-session), cooldowns, dismissal behavior.
- Message types: banner, modal, tooltip/nudge (anchor selector), inbox list.
- Content: rich text/MD subset, CTAs (open URL, emit event, open survey).
- Renderer: themeable (CSS vars), accessible (focus trap, ARIA), reduced motion.
- Delivery state persisted client-side with sync to service for reconciliation.

## Surveys & Forms
- Templates: NPS, CSAT, CES, custom (multi-choice, text, scale).
- Branching/skip logic (basic: based on previous answer).
- Caps: per-user, per-time-window; eligibility by segment and URL.
- Storage: responses stored server-side; events to `watchfn` for analytics.

## Feature Flags
- Config service stores flags and rules; publish signed/ETagged config.
- Client eval: local, deterministic hashing; respects prerequisites; supports `context` (traits) for segment matching.
- Exposure events: emit to `watchfn`; include flag key, variation, rule id.
- Offline/bootstrap: embedded payload option; fallback to defaults on fetch failure.

## Feedback Board (Canny-style, unified sources)
- Core CRUD: create/update status, merge duplicates, tag, assign product area.
- Voting: per-user; prevent multi-vote; anonymous allowed if enabled.
- Sources:
  - In-app submissions.
  - Discord: via `botfn` polling/webhooks; map threads/messages to feedback items.
  - GitHub Discussions: via `plugfn`/webhook; map discussion to feedback.
  - Discourse: via webhook.
  - Email/form: inbound webhook to create feedback.
- Deduplication: title/body similarity; manual merge; store `duplicates` list.
- Surfacing: embeddable board widget with filters (status, tag, product area).

## Roadmap & Changelog
- Roadmap: lanes (Planned/In Progress/Done); cards link to feedback and flags; optional ETA/owner.

# AuthFn feedback acceptance — 2026-10-20

This follow-up closes the prior fixture-only AuthFn compatibility gate for the local repository source path. `npm run test:authfn --workspace=@userfn/service` passes one focused integration acceptance. No UserFn production implementation changes were needed.

The test instantiates the actual `authfn({plugins: [authFnApiKeyPlugin()]}).createServer(...)`, creates a user and real cookie session through AuthFn core APIs, then issues keys through the plugin's POST `/auth/api-keys` route using the session cookie and CSRF token. The actual provider verifies the generated secret, loads its hashed record and updates last-used state. UserFn uses that provider directly with an explicit trusted key-ID-to-tenant resolver and the key's verified scopes.

Acceptance covers:

- AuthFn-issued key produces a committed feedback receipt and authoritative key actor ID.
- Client identity/traits and spoofed tenant/actor headers do not override server authority; top-level tenant payload injection returns 400.
- Same idempotency key is isolated between two tenants; cross-tenant read returns 404.

The existing toast renderer interpreted campaign title/body strings as HTML, whereas the modal renderer already treated those fields as text. The public campaign action callback also assigned arbitrary CTA URLs to `window.location`. ## Reproduction and corrected behavior Actual Chrome 154.0.8037.58 reproduced both title and body `` execution through `UserFnClient.setCampaigns` → `trigger` → inbox-item toast, and execution of a `javascript:` modal CTA. The pre-change built SDK was exercised with `verify-renderer-browser.mjs --expect-vulnerable`; both witnesses executed. Toast title/body now use DOM text nodes, matching existing modal string behavior. The hostile markup is displayed literally and creates no image/SVG nodes or event handlers. No HTML/Markdown sanitizer or parser is being claimed. Existing users who put HTML markup in toast strings now see literal markup; this intentional security correction does not remove a supported typed rich-content format. The original specification's explicit safe rich-text/Markdown subset remains unimplemented and must be designed/tested before enabling formatted content. CTA navigation resolves against the current page URL and permits HTTP, HTTPS, mailto and tel. Relative paths, query/fragment links and protocol-relative HTTP(S) links remain supported. Script/data/file/blob/unknown schemes and malformed URLs are rejected. Checks run at interaction time and again at the public navigation boundary, so mutation of a previously valid campaign URL cannot bypass the guard. Invalid destinations do not invoke the renderer action callback or navigate.
